subject: Subscription Flex-Path & Efficiency Credits — proposal and quant guidance
messages:

Subject: Exploring a subscription path + credits for caching/quantization

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers looked promising. Our procurement and infra leads want to understand how Redwood would structure a commercial pilot that prioritizes both unit-cost reduction and predictable spend. A few asks from our side: 

- Can you sketch a subscription-style alternative to pure PAYG (commit bands, rollover credits, monthly smoothing)?
- What kinds of ‘efficiency credits’ can Redwood offer tied to caching and batching adoption (e.g., prefix cache credits, KV-cache credits)?
- Any high-level quantization recommendations for Llama2-70B and MPT-30B workloads that balance token-cost savings versus latency/regression risk?

We’re aiming for a 3-month pilot with ~3M tokens/day average, peaking to ~8M on heavy days. Happy to jump on a short call.

Best,
Samir
VP of Platform
Aurora AI
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-03-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring a subscription path + credits for caching/quantization

Hi Samir — great questions, thanks. I pulled together an initial commercial sketch (attached) and a few recommendations below; tagging Karthik and Dylan for technical/ops detail.

Short answers up front:
- Subscription Flex-Path: a monthly committed subscription with three rolling bands (Starter / Growth / Scale). Each band contains a token commit, a fixed monthly seat/access fee, and a pool of “efficiency credits” that are redeemable when you adopt KV/prefix caching and continuous batching rules we define. Unused committed tokens can roll for one billing period.
- Efficiency credits: applied as a billing offset when we measure cache hit rates or batching levels above agreed thresholds. Example: 10% cache-hit -> 8% credit applied to token usage for that billing period.
- Quantization: for your MPT-30B baseline we recommend a conservative int8 profile for pilot; for Llama2-70B we suggest an evaluated Q4 profile with a small eval set to check for metric regressions. Expected cost reduction range: 25–45% depending on model and prompt length.

Proposed next steps:
1) We’ll send a Flex-Path pricing spreadsheet with three starter bands for you to review (attached).
2) Karthik will outline the quantization and perf guardrails we require to include quant credits during the pilot.
3) If that looks good, we’ll draft a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) for the 3-month pilot.

Files attached: FlexPath_Prices_v2.xlsx, quant_profiles_summary.pdf

Would you be free for a 30-min sync on Friday?

Cheers,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

On Wed, Mar 22, 2028 at 11:03 -07:00 Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Short answers up front: ...

Hi team — quick technical addendum to make the commercial terms deliverable without surprise: 

1) Quantization profiles: for a pilot we recommend: 
   - MPT-30B: QAT-tested int8 profile (inference-only) — this yields stable throughput and ~30% token-cost reduction on our infra for typical convo lengths.
   - Llama2-70B: Q4-style profile with a staged rollout (A/B eval on 10k prompts). Expect larger variance; plan for a rollback plan if eval metrics degrade.

2) Cache/batch measurement windows: credits should be calculated from a rolling 7-day window to avoid gamed spikes. We will export per-route cache-hit and batching histograms that map to credit tiers.

3) Latency/regression guardrails: quant credits are conditional on passing an automated regression suite (prompt set + latency SLA). If quantized model fails regression, we suspend quant credits until fixes are applied.

4) Ops notes: we can enable automatic fallback to a non-quantized variant for critical routes — this will preserve UX during transient regressions but reduces credit capture while fallbacks are active.

I can put example numbers into the FlexPath spreadsheet if you want — e.g., if cache-hit >= 30% then additional 5% credit; >60% -> 12% credit, etc.

-Karthik
Principal Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference
